new.title: Walk the ruins of Old Smyrna on Tepekule hill
new.desc: Bayrakli Hoyuk (Tepekule) is the site of the original Smyrna, settled since the 3rd millennium BC and later an Ionian city. Excavations uncovered the remains of a temple of Athena from the 7th-6th centuries BC, among the oldest in Anatolia, plus town walls and house foundations.
new.tip: Open-air site with signposted paths and bilingual panels; go in the morning or late afternoon. Reach it by IZBAN to Bayrakli and a short walk or taxi.
new.q: Eski Smyrna Antik Kenti, Tepekule, Bayraklı, İzmir

new.title: See the Folkart Towers rise over Bayraklı
new.desc: Folkart Towers are twin residential skyscrapers in Bayraklı, finished around 2014 and among the tallest buildings in İzmir. They anchor the Bayraklı business district that has grown on the northern bay shore since the 2000s.
new.tip: Best photographed from the Karşıyaka or Konak waterfront, or from the Bayraklı İZBAN station area. The district is built up, so look rather than linger.
new.q: Folkart Towers, Adalet Mahallesi, Manas Bulvarı, Bayraklı, İzmir

new.title: Admire the Karşıyaka Ferry Terminal building
new.desc: Karşıyaka Ferry Terminal is the main pier on the northern shore of the gulf, serving boats to Konak, Alsancak and Pasaport. The building and the waterfront promenade beside it are the social centre of the district.
new.tip: Arrive a little early and sit on the promenade. Look across the gulf to Konak and the Kadifekale hill.

new.title: Visit the historic Karşıyaka railway station
new.desc: Karşıyaka station sits on the suburban line toward Menemen that grew from the 19th-century railways of the Smyrna region, which opened up the northern shore for the city's merchant families. It is now part of the İZBAN network.
new.tip: Take İZBAN here from Alsancak or Bayraklı. The station is a few minutes' walk from the pier.

new.title: Find Latife Hanım Mansion in Karşıyaka
new.desc: Latife Hanım Köşkü is a mansion in Karşıyaka linked to Latife Uşşaki, who was married to Mustafa Kemal Atatürk from 1923 to 1925. The building and its garden are run by the municipality as a small museum and event venue.
new.tip: Check opening times before visiting; it is usually quiet on weekdays.

new.title: Wander Karşıyaka's Levantine streets and mansions
new.desc: Karşıyaka grew in the 19th century as a summer retreat for Levantine and Greek families, and some of their stone and wooden mansions still stand behind the promenade. The streets around Kemalpaşa Caddesi show the layers of that history.
new.tip: Walk from the pier inland along the side streets. Late afternoon light is best.

new.title: See the Levantine pavilions on the Ege University campus
new.desc: The Ege University Bornova campus incorporates restored 19th-century Levantine mansions, including the Wilkinson Residence of 1865, now used by the Rectorate. The Pandispanian Pavilion is a café-restaurant open to staff and visitors.
new.tip: Walk in from the main gate; ask at the café for access to the grounds.

new.title: Look at the Green Mansion in Bornova
new.desc: Green Mansion (Yeşil Köşk) is a 19th-century Levantine house in Bornova that served as the Ege University guesthouse after a 1986 restoration. It was restored again in 1993, 1995 and 2004.
new.tip: Access is limited as the university uses it; look from outside and combine with the Bornova mansions walk.

new.title: Walk past the Fontan d'Escalon mansion on 80th Street
new.desc: This Levantine mansion opposite the Ege University Rectorate was built around 1800 by Fontan d'Escalon, according to the provincial tourism directorate. It is one of the oldest of Bornova's mansions and has been restored.
new.tip: Part of the Mansions District walk. Visit in daylight when the street is quiet.

new.title: See the Charnaud Mansion, now Villa Levante
new.desc: Villa Levante occupies the Charnaud Mansion, one of the best-known Levantine houses in Bornova, converted into a boutique hotel and restaurant. It shows how the Anglo-Levantine merchant families lived in the 19th century.
new.tip: Visit for a coffee or meal to see the interior; reserve for dinner.

new.title: Browse the Ege University Natural History Museum
new.desc: The Natural History Museum of Ege University in Bornova holds large zoological, botanical and geological collections used for teaching and public education. It is among the older university natural history museums in Turkey.
new.tip: Check opening days before going; it suits a rainy morning. Combine with the campus pavilions.
new.q: Ege Üniversitesi Doğa Tarihi Müzesi, Bornova, İzmir

new.title: Visit Yeşilova Höyük, İzmir's 8,500-year-old village
new.desc: Yeşilova Höyük is a Neolithic mound in Bornova inhabited from roughly 6500 BC, regarded as the earliest known settlement in the İzmir area. Ege University excavations continue with support from the Bornova and İzmir municipalities.
new.tip: Check the excavation season and visitor arrangements; finds are shown in municipal exhibitions.

new.title: Stroll Homeros Valley in Bornova
new.desc: Homeros Vadisi in Bornova is a green valley linked by local tradition with the poet Homer, who by some accounts was born in the Smyrna area. A monument commemorates him, and the valley is part of the Bornova culture trail.
new.tip: Go in spring or autumn for walking; it forms a trail with Yeşilova Höyük and the mansions.

new.title: Relax in Hasanağa Gardens in Buca
new.desc: Hasanağa Bahçesi is a large public garden in Buca of about 96,000 square metres, acquired for public use in 1925 and recently renovated. It has old trees, paths and picnic lawns.
new.tip: Free and open year-round; best on spring weekends. Take the metro or a bus to Buca.

new.title: See the animals at İzmir Wildlife Park
new.desc: İzmir Wildlife Park (Sasalı Natural Life Park) opened in 2008 on about 425,000 square metres in Çiğli, replacing the old city zoo. It houses well over a thousand animals of more than 130 species, including giraffes and big cats, in large natural-style enclosures.
new.tip: Open daily; a visit takes half a day. Check ticket prices and the shuttle on the official site.
new.q: İzmir Doğal Yaşam Parkı, Sasalı, Çiğli, İzmir

new.title: Watch flamingos in the Gediz Delta
new.desc: The Gediz Delta is a Ramsar wetland of roughly 14,900 hectares at the head of the Gulf of İzmir and one of the key flamingo breeding sites of the region. A man-made nesting island built in 2012 shelters thousands of flamingo chicks each spring.
new.tip: Best from March to June for chicks and from autumn to spring for flocks; bring binoculars and check access with İzDoğa.

new.title: See the Çamaltı Saltpans at sunset
new.desc: Çamaltı Saltpan in Çiğli lies within the Gediz Delta and has produced sea salt for generations. Its shallow pools attract flamingos, pelicans and herons and glow pink in the evening light.
new.tip: Go late afternoon for the light; roads are rough so a car or a tour is easiest.

new.title: Eat a hot kumru at Kumrucu Ömür in Bostanlı
new.desc: Kumrucu Ömür is a well-known kumru place in Bostanlı, filling a toasted roll with sucuk, salami and melted kaşar, a speciality of İzmir. Local guides often name it among the best in Karşıyaka.
new.tip: Order the mixed kumru with a cold ayran. Expect a queue at weekends.
new.q: Kumrucu Ömür, Cemal Gürsel Caddesi, Bostanlı, Karşıyaka, İzmir

new.title: Grab a kumru at Karşıyaka Kumrucusu by the Çarşı
new.desc: Karşıyaka Kumrucusu serves İzmir's toasted kumru at the entrance of the Çarşı car park, a few steps from the bazaar. It is a quick local lunch stop.
new.tip: Eat it at lunchtime and ask for pickles on the side.
new.q: Karşıyaka Kumrucusu, Çarşı Otopark, Karşıyaka, İzmir

new.title: Finish with baklava and ice cream at Sultan, Bostanlı
new.desc: Sultan Baklava Dondurma in Bostanlı is a popular dessert place with a long ice cream menu alongside baklava. It is a classic stop after a seafront walk.
new.tip: Try pistachio baklava with a scoop of ice cream.
new.q: Sultan Baklava Dondurma, Bostanlı, Karşıyaka, İzmir

new.title: Taste yoghurt ice cream at Bravo Pastanesi
new.desc: Bravo Pastanesi is an İzmir patisserie known for its yoghurt ice cream and wide pastry range. It is one of the long-standing sweet shops of the northern shore.
new.tip: Ask for the yoghurt ice cream; it is busiest after dinner.

new.title: Order a döner at Sakıpağa Dönerevi in the Çarşı
new.desc: Sakıpağa Dönerevi is a döner restaurant inside Karşıyaka Çarşısı, named in local food guides. It is a classic bazaar lunch.
new.tip: Go at midday and order the döner on bread with tomato and pepper.
new.q: Sakıpağa Dönerevi, Karşıyaka Çarşı, Karşıyaka, İzmir

new.title: Eat grilled köfte at Köfteci Erol in Karşıyaka
new.desc: Köfteci Erol is a köfte restaurant in Karşıyaka's Çarşı area, listed in Karşıyaka food guides. It serves grilled meatballs with piyaz.
new.tip: Order the köfte with piyaz and ayran.
new.q: Köfteci Erol, Karşıyaka Çarşı, Karşıyaka, İzmir

new.title: Dine on fresh fish at Boğaziçi, Bostanlı
new.desc: Boğaziçi Restaurant on Cengiz Topel Caddesi is a Bostanlı fish restaurant favoured by local families. Whole fish is priced by weight.
new.tip: Ask the price per kilo before ordering.
new.q: Boğaziçi Restoran, Cengiz Topel Caddesi, Bostanlı, Karşıyaka, İzmir

new.title: Meze and rakı at Karaf Meyhane in Bostanlı
new.desc: Karaf Meyhane is a Bostanlı waterfront meyhane known for its meze and fish. It is among the places locals recommend for an evening out.
new.tip: Book for weekend evenings and share a meze table.

new.title: Eat seafood at Mavra Restaurant on Cemal Gürsel
new.desc: Mavra Restaurant is a seafood restaurant on Cemal Gürsel Caddesi in Bostanlı, close to the sea front.
new.tip: Choose the fish of the day and reserve at weekends.
new.q: Mavra Restaurant, Cemal Gürsel Caddesi, Bostanlı, Karşıyaka, İzmir

new.title: Sip local wine at Kuntra Wine Bar in Bostanlı
new.desc: Kuntra Wine Bar in Bostanlı pairs Turkish wines from the Aegean with small plates. It suits a relaxed evening after the sunset.
new.tip: Ask for a glass of local Urla or Çeşme wine.
new.q: Kuntra Wine Bar, Bostanlı, Karşıyaka, İzmir

new.title: Have tea in the garden of 1912 Asmalı, Karşıyaka
new.desc: 1912 Asmalı is a café-restaurant in a historic Karşıyaka house with a vine-covered garden, written up in the İzmir press as a calm spot in the centre. It is open for breakfast and dinner.
new.tip: Go for breakfast in the garden on a warm day.

new.title: Eat kokoreç at Kokorecci Asim Usta, Bornova
new.desc: Kokorecci Asim Usta on Burak Reis Caddesi is a casual street-food spot in Bornova known for kokoreç, grilled seasoned lamb intestines in a roll. Students and regulars come here late.
new.tip: Order a half portion in a roll with spices; no reservation needed.
new.q: Kokorecci Asim Usta, Burak Reis Caddesi, Bornova, İzmir

new.title: Try the kebap at Emektar Kebap in Bornova
new.desc: Emektar Kebap is a budget kebap house in Bornova listed in the Michelin Guide as an Inspectors favourite. It is well known among locals and students.
new.tip: Order the mixed grill; expect crowds at lunch.

new.title: Spend an evening at Buzuki Meyhane in Bornova
new.desc: Buzuki Meyhane on Süvari Caddesi is a Bornova meyhane popular with students and locals for meze and rakı evenings.
new.tip: Book for weekend evenings.
new.q: Buzuki Meyhane, Süvari Caddesi, Bornova, İzmir

new.title: Have a big breakfast at Mestorant in Bornova
new.desc: Mestorant is a Bornova restaurant with strong reviews for its Turkish breakfast spread, popular with students and families.
new.tip: Go on weekend mornings and arrive early.

new.title: Try söğüş at İkizler Kasap in Buca
new.desc: İkizler Kasap on Hatboyu Caddesi near Buca Hipodrom serves söğüş, cold sliced meat, a traditional İzmir breakfast eaten with vinegared piyaz.
new.tip: Visit on a weekend morning and ask for the piyaz.
new.q: İkizler Kasap, Hatboyu Caddesi, Buca, İzmir

new.title: Eat Bergama köfte in Buca
new.desc: Bergama Köftecisi in Buca serves Bergama-style köfte, a regional meatball style from the Bergama area north of İzmir.
new.tip: Order the köfte portion with salad.

new.title: Taste Buca-style kokoreç at Kazım Usta
new.desc: Kazım Usta has made kokoreç in Buca for about 40 years according to Milliyet, preparing a style local to the district.
new.tip: Eat it as a sandwich; expect lunchtime queues.

new.title: Watch the sunset from the Bostanlı sunset terrace
new.desc: Bostanlı Gün Batımı Seyir Terası is a timber waterfront terrace on the northern shore, designed as part of the İzmirSea coastal regeneration project, facing west across the Gulf of İzmir.
new.tip: Arrive 45 to 60 minutes before sunset in summer; free.
new.q: Bostanlı Gün Batımı Terası, Bostanlı, Karşıyaka, İzmir

new.title: Cycle the bay path from Karşıyaka to Mavişehir
new.desc: A flat waterfront cycling and walking path runs along the northern shore of the gulf from Karşıyaka through Bostanlı toward Mavişehir, passing parks and the sunset terrace.
new.tip: Ride in the evening for cooler air and views; allow an hour each way.
new.q: Karşıyaka Sahil Bisiklet Yolu, Karşıyaka, İzmir

new.title: Browse the pedestrian Karşıyaka Çarşı bazaar
new.desc: Karşıyaka Çarşı is a pedestrianised shopping district with shops, traditional bakeries and cafés, a few streets from the pier.
new.tip: Buy boyoz at a bakery and eat it on the promenade.

new.title: Catch a Karşıyaka SK football match
new.desc: Karşıyaka SK is one of İzmir's oldest football clubs, with a passionate following known for its atmosphere. Home games are played at the Karşıyaka stadium.
new.tip: Buy tickets in advance for big games and check fixtures.

new.title: See a Karşıyaka basketball game at the arena
new.desc: Pınar Karşıyaka is one of Turkey's leading basketball clubs, and its home games are played at the Karşıyaka Arena.
new.tip: Check fixtures and buy tickets in advance.

new.title: Catch a summer concert at Suat Taşer Open Air Theatre
new.desc: Bostanlı Suat Taşer Open Air Theatre hosts concerts and theatre by the sea in Bostanlı, mostly in the summer months.
new.tip: Check the municipal programme for dates.
new.q: Suat Taşer Açık Hava Tiyatrosu, Bostanlı, Karşıyaka, İzmir

new.title: Join the İzDoğa Flamingo Road tour
new.desc: The Flamingo Road is a guided tour by İzDoğa along the Gediz coast and the Kaklıç and Degaj routes, departing from the Wildlife Park in Sasalı.
new.tip: Book ahead and bring binoculars.
new.q: Doğal Yaşam Parkı, Sasalı, Çiğli, İzmir

new.title: Visit İzmir Bird Paradise at Çamaltı
new.desc: İzmir Bird Paradise is the managed bird sanctuary in the Çamaltı Saltpan area of Çiğli, within the Ramsar-listed Gediz Delta, with pelicans and flamingos.
new.tip: Spring and autumn are best; check opening arrangements first.
new.q: İzmir Kuş Cenneti, Çamaltı, Çiğli, İzmir

new.title: Cycle and picnic in the Sasalı pine woods
new.desc: Sasalı Picnic Area is a 750,000 square metre green space of pines with walking and cycling tracks, next to the Wildlife Park.
new.tip: Free; busy on weekends.
new.q: Sasalı Piknik Alanı, Sasalı, Çiğli, İzmir

new.title: Walk around Buca Pond and its cafés
new.desc: Buca Göleti is a 167,000 square metre recreation area with cafés, an amphitheatre and walking paths.
new.tip: Visit on summer evenings.

new.title: Walk the mansions of Bornova's 80th Street
new.desc: The Mansions District around 80th Street opposite Ege University is covered by Bornova municipality's heritage project.
new.tip: Combine with the Ege campus.

new.title: Browse the Bornova çarşı and Republic Square
new.desc: Bornova's old bazaar is being renewed as part of the 'heart of Bornova' project, leading toward Cumhuriyet Square.
new.tip: Reach it by the metro to Bornova.

new.title: Follow the Bornova Culture Island trail
new.desc: A trail linking the Levantine mansions, Yeşilova Höyük and Homeros Valley was signed as the Bornova Culture Island project in 2022.
new.tip: Allow half a day.

new.title: Stroll the Mavişehir waterfront
new.desc: Mavişehir is a planned district on the northern shore with a long promenade and parks, near the Gediz delta wetlands.
new.tip: Good at sunset.

new.title: Relax in Karşıyaka Human Rights Park
new.desc: İnsan Hakları Parkı is a seafront park in Karşıyaka, listed in guides as a spot for strolls.
new.tip: Free.
